items.headline: Sensex flat at 73,598.67 and Nifty at 22,749.75 ahead of the Fed; midcaps gain 1%
items.summary: A volatile session ended largely unchanged as bank and IT profit-taking offset gains in pharma, realty and consumer durables. Follows Monday's break of a four-day losing streak. Stabilising.
items.rationale: Crude near $114 and caution before the Fed decision cap large caps, while broader-market buying shows domestic demand for stocks remains intact.

items.headline: Foreign investors buy a net ₹4,240 crore; domestic funds sell ₹1,250 crore (provisional)
items.summary: A reversal from Monday's ₹1,462 crore foreign selling. October outflows had topped ₹48,000 crore. Figures come from provisional exchange data. Reversing, for now.
items.rationale: A day of foreign buying supports heavyweights and the rupee, but one session does not change a month of heavy outflows driven by oil.

items.headline: Brent settles 1.7% lower at $113.88 as Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey agree to keep talking
items.summary: WTI settled at $99.90. Profit-taking followed the run above $117. The US says it is 'decision time' on Iran and keeps blockading Iranian ports. Second day of easing.
items.rationale: Every dollar off crude trims India's import bill and fuel subsidy risk, but prices near $114 still keep inflation and the current account under strain.

items.headline: Rupee edges up 3 paise to 95.12 per dollar on likely RBI intervention
items.summary: It traded between 95.09 and 95.24 as the dollar firmed before the Fed decision. Ongoing pressure near record lows, held in check by the RBI.
items.rationale: A weak rupee raises the cost of imported oil and inputs; RBI dollar sales steady the currency but draw down reserves.

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield holds near a three-year high; data providers show 7.44–7.49%
items.summary: Monday's 7.48% close was the highest since 2022. Markets price slightly more than 100 basis points of RBI hikes over 12 months. Ongoing.
items.rationale: High yields raise borrowing costs for the government, companies and home buyers, and weigh on banks' bond holdings.

items.headline: Fed meeting begins; 94 of 100 economists expect a hold at 3.75–4.00%, all see a December hike
items.summary: US inflation rose to 3.7% in September while payrolls grew only 29,000. Decision due 28 October, 18:00 GMT; hawkish dissents possible. Ongoing.
items.rationale: A hold is priced in, but a firm signal of a December hike would strengthen the dollar and US yields, adding pressure on the rupee, G-Secs and foreign flows.

items.headline: Oil minister says India faces no US pressure on Russian oil; refiners buying more discounted Gulf crude
items.summary: Refiners will buy on commercial terms; Russian purchases have fallen as Gulf grades sell at a discount. Middle Eastern imports returned to pre-war levels in September. Continues the shift reported yesterday.
items.rationale: Sourcing on price limits the import bill and lowers sanctions and tariff risk with the US, though it raises reliance on Gulf routes exposed to Hormuz.

items.headline: September factory output growth seen slowing to about 6% from 8%; capital goods 2.2% vs 16.9%
items.summary: A lender's forecast ahead of the official release sees mining shrinking about 8% and electricity up about 15.6%. New indicator for the week.
items.rationale: A sharp capital goods slowdown would signal weaker investment as oil and higher rates bite, weighing on industrials and growth estimates.
